questions.q: What is the core difference between a formatter like `black` and a linter like `ruff`?
options: There is no real difference — they do the same thing
A linter rewrites code; a formatter only reports problems
Formatters only work on JavaScript, not Python
A formatter automatically rewrites code style; a linter reports problems (like unused imports or undefined names) without rewriting the code
questions.explain: black is a formatter: it changes how code looks (whitespace, quotes, line breaks) automatically. ruff is a linter: it analyzes code and reports issues like unused imports or undefined names without changing the file itself.

questions.q: Why is `black` described as "deliberately almost non-configurable"?
options: So that teams stop spending time debating style choices — everyone's code ends up in the same consistent format with no settings to argue over
Because the developers were too lazy to add options
Because configuration options would make it too slow
It is actually highly configurable, with hundreds of settings
questions.explain: black intentionally limits configuration options. The goal isn't that its particular style is objectively superior — it's to eliminate time spent debating formatting preferences on a team, since there's little left to configure.

questions.q: In the lesson's ruff example, what does the `F821` warning on `retrun data` indicate?
options: That the line has incorrect indentation
That `retrun` is an undefined name — almost certainly a typo for `return`
That the function load_config is unused
That json.load requires two arguments
questions.explain: F821 flags an undefined name. Since `retrun` isn't a valid Python keyword or a variable that was ever defined, ruff correctly identifies it as an undefined name — in this case a typo for the `return` keyword.

questions.q: What does the `F401` warning mean when ruff reports `'os' imported but unused`?
options: The os module doesn't exist in Python
The os module was imported twice
The os module was imported at the top of the file but never actually used anywhere in the code
The os module is deprecated and should not be used
questions.explain: F401 flags an import that was never referenced anywhere else in the file. Unused imports clutter code and can hide actual mistakes, so linters flag them by default.

questions.q: Why do both `black` and `ruff` read their settings from a shared `pyproject.toml` file checked into the repository?
options: Because Python requires all configuration to live in one file
pyproject.toml is only used for installing dependencies, not for black or ruff
To make the tools run faster
So every contributor and every CI run applies the exact same formatting and linting rules, instead of each developer's local settings differing
questions.explain: Keeping tool configuration in a shared, version-controlled file ensures consistency: everyone on the team, and every automated CI check, enforces the identical set of formatting and linting rules rather than relying on individual local setups.
